statements.subject: client
statements.description: A Transport request-header MAY contain a list of transport options acceptable to the client, in the form of multiple transport specification entries.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A Transport request-header MAY contain multiple transport specifications using the same transport protocol identifier.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST return a Transport response-header in the response to indicate the values actually chosen, if any.
actions: include Transport response-header in SETUP response indicating chosen values

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If no transport specification is supported, no transport header is returned and the response MUST use the status code 461 (Unsupported Transport) (Section 17.4.25).
actions: send 461 Unsupported Transport response
omit Transport header from response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In case more than one transport specification was present in the request, the server MUST return the single transport specification (transport-spec) that was actually chosen, if any.
actions: return single chosen transport-spec in SETUP response

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Transport header MAY also be used in subsequent SETUP requests to change transport parameters.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY refuse to change parameters of an existing stream.
actions: refuse to change transport parameters of existing stream

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Each transport protocol identifier defines the parameters that are required to occur; additional optional parameters MAY occur.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Parameters MAY be given in any order.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The transport protocol identifier, and all parameters, need to be understood in a transport specification; if not, the transport specification MUST be ignored.
actions: ignore transport specification with unknown identifier or parameters

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: An RTSP proxy of any type that uses or modifies the transport specification, e.g., access proxy or security proxy, MUST remove specifications with unknown parameters before forwarding the RTSP message.
actions: remove transport specifications with unknown parameters before forwarding message

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: If that results in no remaining transport specification, the proxy SHALL send a 461 (Unsupported Transport) (Section 17.4.25) response without any Transport header.
actions: send 461 Unsupported Transport response without Transport header

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The lack of the dest_addr parameter indicates that the server MUST send media to the same address from which the RTSP messages originates.
actions: send media to RTSP message originating address

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST include the information if it is available in the session description.
actions: include multicast address information from session description in Transport header

statements.subject: message
statements.description: One of the two values MUST be specified.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client originating the RTSP request MAY specify the destination address of the stream recipient with the host address as part of the tuple.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: To avoid becoming the unwitting perpetrator of a remote-controlled DoS attack, a server MUST perform security checks (see Section 21.2.1) and SHOULD log such attempts before allowing the client to direct a media stream to a recipient address not chosen by the server.
actions: perform security checks per Section 21.2.1 before allowing media delivery to non-server-chosen address

statements.subject: server
statements.description: To avoid becoming the unwitting perpetrator of a remote-controlled DoS attack, a server MUST perform security checks (see Section 21.2.1) and SHOULD log such attempts before allowing the client to direct a media stream to a recipient address not chosen by the server.
actions: log such attempts before allowing media delivery to non-server-chosen address

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server does not allow the host address part of the tuple to be set, it MUST return 463 (Destination Prohibited).
actions: send 463 Destination Prohibited response

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The host address part of the tuple MAY be empty, for example ":58044", in cases when it is desired to specify only the destination port.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Responses to requests including the Transport header with a dest_addr parameter SHOULD include the full destination address that is actually used by the server.
actions: include full destination address actually used by server in Transport response header

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST NOT remove address information that is already present in the request when responding, unless the protocol requires it.
actions: preserve address information from request in Transport response header

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This parameter MUST be specified by the server if it transmits media packets from an address other than the one RTSP messages are sent to.
actions: specify src_addr parameter in Transport response header

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The address or addresses indicated in the src_addr parameter SHOULD be used both for the sending and receiving of the media stream's data packets.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The argument provides the channel number to be used in the $ block (see Section 14) and MUST be present.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: This parameter MAY be specified as an interval, e.g., interleaved=4-5 in cases where the transport choice for the media stream requires it, e.g., for RTP with RTCP.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MAY set any valid channel number in the response.

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: The declared channels are bidirectional, so both end parties MAY send data on the given channel.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The binary MIKEY message SHALL be Base64-encoded [RFC4648] before being included in the value part of the parameter, where the encoding adheres to the definition in Section 4 of RFC 4648 and where the padding bits are set to zero.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: These parameters MAY only be used if the media-transport protocol is RTP.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The ssrc parameter MUST NOT be specified in requests.
actions: omit ssrc parameter from SETUP request Transport header

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the parameter is included in the Transport header of a SETUP request, the server SHOULD ignore it, and choose appropriate SSRCs for the stream.
actions: ignore ssrc parameter in SETUP request
choose appropriate SSRCs for stream

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server SHOULD set the ssrc parameter in the Transport header of the response.
actions: include ssrc parameter in Transport response header

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHALL only include one transport stream in the Transport header specification.
actions: include only one transport stream in Transport header when RTCP-mux parameter is present

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The parameter setup and connection defined below MAY only be used if the media-transport protocol of the lower-level transport is connection oriented (such as TCP).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: However, these parameters MUST NOT be used when interleaving data over the RTSP connection.
actions: omit setup and connection parameters from Transport header when interleaving data over RTSP connection

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In response to a client SETUP request where the setup parameter is set to "active", a server's 2xx reply MUST assign the setup parameter to "passive" on the Transport header line.
actions: assign setup=passive in Transport response header

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In response to a client SETUP request where the setup parameter is set to "passive", a server's 2xx reply MUST assign the setup parameter to "active" on the Transport header line.
actions: assign setup=active in Transport response header

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In response to a client SETUP request where the setup parameter is set to "actpass", a server's 2xx reply MUST assign the setup parameter to "active" or "passive" on the Transport header line.
actions: assign setup=active or setup=passive in Transport response header

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: Note that the "holdconn" value for setup is not defined for RTSP use, and MUST NOT appear on a Transport line.
actions: prohibit use of holdconn value in Transport setup parameter

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a client SETUP request assigns the "new" value to "connection", the server response MUST also assign the "new" value to "connection" on the Transport line.
actions: assign connection=new in Transport response header

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a client SETUP request assigns the "existing" value to "connection", the server response MUST assign a value of "existing" or "new" to "connection" on the Transport line, at its discretion.
actions: assign connection=existing or connection=new in Transport response header at server's discretion
